speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe how this lesion started and if you have noticed any changes in its size or appearance over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease, I need to determine if this is a manifestation of your underlying condition. Does the lesion feel like a deep, burning pain, and have you noticed any new gastrointestinal symptoms or joint pain recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a painful ulcer with purplish irregular borders and a history of trauma, combined with your Crohn's disease, strongly suggests Pyoderma Gangrenosum rather than simple cellulitis. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin_Biopsy: Histopathology findings show neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.
